projects.title: Ledger
projects.description: Invoices and hours for a small studio. It replaced three spreadsheets and one notebook nobody could read.
projects.ai:
Claude wrote the first pass of the invoice parser. I rewrote the edge cases: VAT on partial hours, credit notes, the client who pays in two halves.

Cursor did most of the boring CRUD while I watched the tests. When it got clever with the database, I made it boring again.

The numbers are mine. I checked every total by hand for the first two months.

projects.title: Olive Mill
projects.description: Shop for a family olive-oil mill. Two products, one checkout, nothing else on purpose.
projects.ai:
I used Claude to draft the product copy in three languages, then the family rewrote half of it because "nobody talks like that about oil".

The checkout is hand-written. I asked the model for help with the shipping rules and kept only the tests it suggested.

projects.title: Rollcall
projects.description: Attendance for university classes. Students scan a code, I stop counting heads.
projects.ai:
Claude Code scaffolded the QR flow and the export to the university spreadsheet in an afternoon. The afternoon after that I spent removing what it added "just in case".

An n8n flow sends the weekly attendance summary. A model writes the one-line comment at the top; I read it before it goes out.

No student data goes to any model. That was the first rule, before any code.

projects.title: Type Check
projects.description: WordPress plugin that flags orphaned words and bad hyphenation before anyone presses publish.
projects.ai:
The hyphenation rules come from books, not from a model. I used Claude to turn my notes into test cases, about two hundred of them.

Cursor helped with the WordPress hooks I never remember. I reviewed every line before it touched a real site.

projects.title: Seat Map
projects.description: Seat booking for a small theatre. Runs fine on the box-office laptop from 2014.
projects.ai:
The seat layout started as a photo of the theatre plan. Claude turned it into JSON; I fixed row K, which does not exist in real life either.

The box-office laptop is from 2014, so I asked for plain JavaScript and said no to every framework it offered. It listened, mostly.

projects.title: Class Notes
projects.description: Course notes for my frontend classes. Plain HTML, updated the night before, as usual.
projects.ai:
I record the class, Whisper transcribes it, and Claude turns the transcript into a first draft of the notes.

Then I cut it in half. Students read short notes; they do not read long ones.

The exercises are mine. The model is good at explaining, not at choosing what is worth practising.
